Executive Summary
This manual operationalizes the curriculum. It defines the 150-lab repository, assessment architecture, evidence 
requirements, interview simulation model, and the final enterprise capstone. Every practical exercise follows a 
build-test-fail-recover-document-cleanup loop.

2. Standard Lab Lifecycle
1.
Define the business scenario and measurable outcome.
2.
Record the starting state, versions and constraints.
3.
Implement the smallest safe solution.
4.
Add repeatable validation and security checks.
5.
Inject a realistic failure.
6.
Diagnose from observable evidence rather than assumptions.
7.
Recover through rollback, restore or remediation.
8.
Document trade-offs and enterprise-scale changes.
9.
Remove temporary resources and prove cleanup.

5. Practical Examination Template

Receive a production scenario, constraints and target outcome.

Create a brief plan and risk assessment before changing the environment.

Implement the solution without copying a complete answer.

Demonstrate tests, logs, failure handling and rollback.

Explain two rejected alternatives and why they were rejected.

Submit evidence and a concise operational handover.

7. Final Enterprise Capstone
The capstone integrates the complete curriculum into a single enterprise delivery platform. The learner builds a 
sample application and the platform needed to develop, secure, deploy, observe, operate and improve it.
Workstream
Required implementation
Source and collaboration
Protected branches, pull requests, reviews and release tags
CI/CD
Test, build, scan, sign, publish, deploy and rollback
Infrastructure
Versioned IaC, environment separation and state protection
Runtime
Containers and Kubernetes with health, scaling and policy
Security
Secrets, least privilege, SBOM, provenance and policy gates

10. Certification and Completion Rules

Completion certificates should represent demonstrated competence, not attendance alone.

The learner must retain evidence for every required practical exam.

Any critical security or cleanup failure requires reattempt.

Capstone acceptance requires both technical demonstration and oral defense.

The final portfolio must include architecture, code, evidence, incident learning and outcomes.
